linkedin.text:
I used to spend 20 minutes every morning re-teaching Claude Code the same architectural patterns.

Then I found ECC.

It's not another AI tool. It's the performance layer that makes AI agents actually persistent.

205,000 stars. 249 skills. Memory that survives sessions.

What changed for me:

→ My AI agent remembers project context automatically
→ Security scanning runs before every commit (AgentShield built-in)
→ Skills continuously improve from past sessions
→ Works across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex — same muscle memory

This repo represents 10 months of real engineering workflows, not hypothetical examples.

The difference between copy-pasting prompts and having an actual agent system? Your AI gets smarter over time instead of resetting every day.

If you're doing serious work with AI agents, this is the missing infrastructure layer.
